controls.name: band
controls.doc: One graphic-EQ fader's travel: EQ_GAIN_RANGE by reference (a graphic fader is an EQ gain), with the come-up value it needs as a row field — flat, 0 dB.

controls.name: mode
controls.doc: How the graphic EQ designs its sections from the faders, in the order of the integer the kernel reads (omx-dsp's enum omx_geq_mode): `standard` gives each section its fader as its gain, the classic proportional build-up; `true` solves the band interaction so the summed curve meets the faders at the centres, each section gain clamped at GEQ_DESIGN_GAIN_MAX_DB. A fresh instance comes up `standard`.

readouts.name: designClamped
readouts.doc: Whether the last design clamped: 1 when a `true` solve asked a section for more than GEQ_DESIGN_GAIN_MAX_DB and got the ceiling, 0 otherwise and always in `standard`. Derived by the design step, never written by a host (omx-dsp's OmxGeqDesign.clamped).

GEQ_BAND_Q.doc: The graphic EQ's band Q: the ISO third-octave bandwidth, `2^(1/6)/(2^(1/3) − 1) ≈ 4.318`, to one decimal as the M32 GEQ carries it. Read by the `geq31` preset and the graphic EQ's section design.

GEQ_PROTO_DB.doc: The prototype gain the `true` solve's first interaction matrix is evaluated at: the middle of the travel's magnitude, where a matched-Z section's dB response per dB of gain is closest to its average.

GEQ_DESIGN_GAIN_MAX_DB.doc: The ceiling on a section gain the `true` solve may ask for: above the travel's worst case (26.0 dB, the alternating ±15 set) with margin. A solve past it clamps and the row says so (`designClamped`), never silently.
